name: Cameroon
summary_text: Cameroon is dangerous for trans visitors. The Shakiro case is the defining documentation: in February 2021, trans women Shakiro and Patricia were arrested in a Douala restaurant for the clothes they were wearing, convicted of “attempted homosexuality,” “indecent dressing” and ID irregularities, and sentenced to five years. They described five months of “hell” in Douala's central prison, initially in leg chains, before release pending appeal; Shakiro later received asylum in Belgium. Article 347-1 criminalises same-sex acts (up to 5 years), and Cameroon has among Africa's highest prosecution rates. Police and mob violence against perceived LGBT people are both documented, and there is no legal gender recognition or protection of any kind. The Shakiro conviction shows that visible trans expression in a public place is itself treated as a prosecutable offence. For a visitor: visible trans presentation in public risks arrest on indecency/ID grounds; prison conditions are severe.

sources.title: Cameroon jails transgender women for 'attempted homosexuality'
sources.claim_summary: BBC (May 2021): two trans women in Cameroon, including trans celebrity YouTuber Shakiro, were sentenced to five years in prison for 'attempted homosexuality', outraging public decency and ID-card problems - the maximum term. Lawyer Alice Nkom: 'The message is clear: homosexuals don't have a place in Cameroon.' Cameroon is among 31 African countries criminalising gay sex.

sources.title: Shakiro - Wikipedia
sources.claim_summary: Wikipedia biography of Shakiro (b. 1997), Cameroonian trans activist: arrested and charged with 'attempted homosexuality' in 2021, sentenced to five years; fled Cameroon later that year, hid in Nigeria, and received asylum in Belgium in 2023.

US State Department 2010 Human Rights Report for Cameroon: documents discrimination against gays and lesbians among societal abuses, alongside security-force killings, torture, harsh prisons, and arbitrary arrests - the criminalisation context (Article 347).
